question.text: A body of weight <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>64</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> is pushed with just enough force to start it moving across a horizontal floor and the same force continues to act afterwards. If the coefficients of static and dynamic friction are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn></math> respectively, the acceleration of the body will be (Acceleration due to gravity = <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
Weight of the body = 64 N 
so the mass of the body m=6.4 kg, μ k =0.4


Net acceleration = Applied force -Kinetic friction Mass of the body = μ s mg− μ k mg m =( μ s − μ k )g=(0.6−0.4)g=0.2 g =2 m s-2
